summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and diabetes was admitted with left-sided chest pain, nausea, and body aches that began two hours after a hemodialysis session. Initial concerns included acute coronary syndrome, but serial cardiac enzymes were normal and EKG changes were stable. The chest pain resolved and did not recur during the hospital stay. Elevated potassium on admission improved with dialysis. A chest X-ray showed new bibasilar opacities, likely atelectasis, with no clinical signs of infection. The patient's symptoms were determined to be non-cardiac, possibly related to dialysis disequilibrium or recent endoscopic procedures. He remained stable, tolerated a light diet, completed a hemodialysis session prior to discharge, and was discharged home in good condition with instructions to continue all home medications and follow up with his specialists.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
